title: Dynamic play

D0.outcome: Explains that dynamic factors (initiative, piece activity, tempo) can outweigh static features such as a damaged pawn structure.

D1.outcome: Given a position with a damaged pawn structure, counts the activity that compensates and states whether it is enough.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, judges when activity outweighs structure and labels the verdict practical or sound.

D3.outcome: Predicts how a single tempo flips a dynamic verdict, and rejects 'damaged structure means worse' without a count.

misconceptions: A damaged pawn structure means an inferior position.
sources: sources/sheets/nimzowitsch_my-system.md §4 idea 47; §7 row 47 (label practical, not sound)
conditions: Piece activity and initiative compensate for the structure (the textbook error in the 1895 Ruy Lopez verdict).
A sacrifice for a blockade is practical, not proven sound, until verified.
contrasts: An early structural damage verdict that the engine reverses through activity.
Treating a positional sacrifice as sound without checking.
A closed position where activity cannot be realised.

soft_prereq_notes.ATK.SUPERIORITY.D3: dynamic play is attack with a count
